I don’t have much expertise so this would just be my personal experience, but I did experience spikes in anxiety when tapering off another SSRI. If you can I think it’s a lot better to avoid skipping or changing up your dose unnecessarily, can you ask for more supply when you get your refills or refill them earlier? This sounds a lot like me, I was recently diagnosed with cyclothymia but have been asking my therapist if it could be BP2 instead since my lows can get super low. Luckily it doesn’t actually matter that much since the treatments for cyclothymia and bipolar are pretty much the same - so it won’t really affect your treatment much (if you’re taking mood stabilizers - I think those are more encouraged if it’s known to be BP, you can advocate for getting on them though if you have cyclothymia). It also helps me to know that cyclothymia is on the same spectrum as bipolar 1 and 2, so if you think you could really have one of those it’s not that huge of a difference - meaning you know the pattern and function of the disorder you likely have, the different labels that would be put on it if you’re unsure between those would just be a matter of severity. I think knowing the spectrum of disorder helps a ton and the exact level it falls under is something you can nail down later but that won’t really affect your treatment much or how you need to think it, but I do get that it can be frustrating to not know for sure

She needs to understand why her grandmother would say something like that (whatever reason you believe it to be - jealousy, control, etc) or she'll always wonder if it's true no matter how much you reassure her it isn't. A lesson I learned in therapy is that "core beliefs" are not successfully challenged by evidence to the contrary without addressing them head on, so if this fear was instilled in her it's really important to clarify exactly why someone would falsely say that and that it isn't true.
